questions.prompt: Your prompt holds instructions, a contract and two example summaries. Why wrap each part in its own tag, like <contract>…</contract>?

options.text: Tags make the model work faster, and they lower the cost of each request.
options.explanation: Tags are about clarity, not speed or price.

options.text: So the model can see where each part starts and ends, and doesn't mix them up.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's guide says separate tags reduce misinterpretation when a prompt mixes instructions, context and examples.

options.text: Models can only read text that is placed inside tags, so untagged text is skipped.
options.explanation: Models read untagged text too. Tags just make the structure clear.

questions.prompt: Which instruction follows the tip in the Claude docs on format?

options.text: "Don't use bullet points or headings, don't be long, and don't use jargon."
options.explanation: This only says what not to do. The guide suggests saying what to do instead.

options.text: "Write three short paragraphs of plain prose, under 150 words in total."
options.explanation: Right. It says what to do, and it is exact about length.

options.text: "Format it nicely and clearly, the way a professional would format it."
options.explanation: This is vague. The model has to guess what "nicely" means.

questions.prompt: Structured outputs make every answer follow your schema. What do they NOT guarantee?

options.text: That every required field is present in the answer.
options.explanation: That is what they are built to guarantee. OpenAI's docs say the model won't omit a required key.

options.text: That the values in the fields are correct.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's docs say structured outputs can still contain mistakes, and Gemini's docs say to always validate the values.

options.text: That the answer is returned as valid JSON.
options.explanation: Valid JSON is part of what they guarantee. The values inside can still be wrong.
